title: Ground a tested bus bar with a two-clamp grounding set, in the safe order
instruction: Ground bar B for work, using the grounding set on the table (bar B is the bar with the yellow TESTED tag). The set's right clamp is its ground end and belongs on the ground bar GND; its left clamp is its line end and belongs on bar B. At the end both clamps must be tight on their bars and neither stick held. Keep both clamps off bars A and C.
context: Before work on de-energised conductors, a protective grounding set is attached to a bar that has been tested dead. The rule (OSHA 29 CFR 1910.269(n)(6)(i)): the ground end is connected first, and the line end only after it, and only to a tested bar; connecting the line end first, or to a bar that was never tested, can put the cable, the set and the worker at the bar's voltage if it is still live. The instruction gives only the goal (the set on bar B, both clamps tight, sticks let go) and the constraints (which clamp is which end, keep off bars A and C); the order is not stated, because knowing it is what the task tests. Procedure, for the reviewer: take the ground clamp (right) by its stick handle, hang it on GND and turn the stick clockwise (seen from above) until the clamp is tight (about 1.5 turns); only then hang the line clamp (left) on bar B and tighten it the same way; let go of both sticks.
setup: Positions are from the arm bases (x: cm in front of the line joining the two bases, which are 61 cm apart; y: cm left (+) or right (-) of their midline, seen from behind the robot; heights above the table top). Back board: an insulating board (dark grey phenolic or plywood) 1.8 cm thick, 12 cm tall and 77 cm wide (y -34 to +43), standing upright on the table, fixed, its front face 29.1 cm in front of the bases; on its top a grey ledge 9 cm deep (from 29.1 to 38.1 cm) and 6 mm thick. Bars: four pieces of 1/4 x 2 in copper bus bar (6.35 x 50.8 mm, Burndy BBB14212P stock, cut to length), lying flat with their wide faces horizontal, back edges against the board, front edges 24 cm in front of the bases, top faces 6.0 cm above the table: the ground bar GND, 12 cm long, centred 16 cm right of the midline, with a green/yellow band on its top face; phase bars A, B and C, each 7 cm long, centred 13.5, 22 and 30.5 cm left. The letters A, B, C and GND are on 2.2 cm labels on the board's face above each bar and on the ledge behind it. TESTED tag: a yellow card 7.2 x 4.4 cm reading TESTED lies flat on the ledge behind bar B (centred 22 cm left, from 33.1 to 37.5 cm in front of the bases). Parking plates: two black insulating plates, 3 mm thick, 5 cm long and as deep as the bars, their tops level with the bar tops: one centred 26 cm right of the midline (the ground clamp's), one 39 cm left (the line clamp's). Grounding set: two C-type grounding clamps with eye screws, CHANCE PSC6003412 class (aluminium C frame 24 mm thick, throat 22 mm deep, serrated hook jaw, bronze 5/8 in eye screw with a swivel pad, 0.77 kg each), joined by a yellow 2/0-class ground cable (16 mm across, 90 cm long) that leaves each clamp straight down from a ferrule behind the jaw and lies on the table in front of the bars. Each clamp is used upside down: hook jaw under the bar, eye screw vertical on top. At the start each clamp hangs, loose, on its parking plate by its pad, its screw axis 2.15 cm behind the plate's front edge, the jaw opening 3 mm wider than a bar. On each eye screw a short stick is fixed (a stick-mounted clamp, Salisbury 1924 class, cut down): a black head 3 cm long, a red collar and a black square handle 2.6 x 2.6 x 5.5 cm, 12 cm in all, the handle's centre 20.9 cm above the table. Turning the stick clockwise (seen from above) drives the pad down; about 1.2 turns close the slack and grip a bar. Both arms start at the ready pose with their grippers open. One fixed layout, as in the screenshot.
scoring: A clamp counts as tight on a bar when the bar is between its jaw and pad and the eye screw has been turned until the pad presses the bar with at least 120 N (about 0.4 N m on the eye screw; checked after the run with a torque screwdriver on the eye: the screw does not turn further below 0.4 N m). A clamp touches a bar when its jaw, spine or pad comes within 2 mm of it (judged from video). Score 0 if at any time a clamp touches bar A or bar C, or a clamp touches any phase bar (A, B or C) while the ground clamp is not yet tight on GND. Otherwise the score is the highest level reached: 0.25 the ground clamp is tight on GND; 0.5 the line clamp is also hung on bar B (the bar between its jaws) while the ground clamp is tight; 0.75 the line clamp is tight on bar B too and both grippers are at least 5 cm from both stick handles; 1.0 the after-release tug check also passes. Tug check, once both clamps have stayed tight with both grippers 5 cm or more from both handles continuously for 1 s (the 1 s restarts if any of this lapses): hook a spring scale on the line clamp's frame and pull it horizontally toward the robot (off the bar's front edge), rising to 40 N over 1 s and held 1.5 s; then the same on the ground clamp. It passes if, throughout each pull, the clamp stays within 3 mm of where it started and on its bar, and both grippers stay 5 cm or more from both handles; otherwise the score is 0.75. The instruction does not state the order; the 0 for touching a phase bar before the ground clamp is tight is what tests it.
reset_notes: Loosen each clamp by turning its stick counterclockwise about 1.5 turns (until the jaw opening is 3 mm wider than the bar), lift the line clamp off bar B and the ground clamp off GND (line end first), and hang each back by its pad on its parking plate with the cable lying on the table in front of the bars as in the setup photo. Check the TESTED tag is on the ledge behind bar B. Nothing is energised at any time. About 2 minutes.
fidelity: PhysX rigid bodies on joints, arms with the station's i2rt gains. Published: clamp jaw range, 28 N·m install torque, bar and cable size; clamp proportions inferred. Screw thread is a rule (pad follows screw angle; friction rises with clamp force). Cable is 18 jointed links. Simplified: 12 cm handle instead of a 1.2-1.8 m stick; reachable torque ~0.6-0.9 N·m so tight = 120 N; clamps upside down on flat bars; tug test in sim after recording. Details in README.
scores: Dream-1 run (with the earlier, procedural instruction; not re-run with the new wording): 0.0 (the arms moved over the bench but neither clamp was picked up); demo (cameras and joint states only): 1.0; control (line clamp hung on B, not tightened): 0.5
